transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-10-10
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Reynolds (NovaSearch Head of Search), Janelle Ortiz (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (Staff Eng)

Summary (auto): quick demo of hosted embeddings + rerank. Showed end-to-end flow: index with embeddings, similarity search, candidate fetch, rerank call to improve relevance. Discussed perf/cost tradeoffs and pilot next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood Inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Mark: Hey Alex, good thanks. Excited to see what you have, we been looking at ways to lift relevance across ecom and docs search.
[00:15] Janelle: Yep hi all. We've got Samir on the call to cover infra questions.
[00:20] Priya (SE): Awesome, quick agenda: 1) high-level API walkthrough for embeddings + rerank, 2) demo in the console and curl examples, 3) talk about perf and caching, 4) security/compliance notes, and 5) next steps. Sound OK?
[00:30] Mark: Yep sounds good.

[02:05] Priya: Alright jumping in - at a high level our Hosted API supports a dedicated embeddings endpoint and a separate rerank endpoint. Typical pattern we show is two-stage retrieval: first dense retrieve via embeddings similarity, then call /rerank to reorder top-K with the full context and prompt.
[02:25] Mark: When you say embeddings endpoint, is that just a vector store or do you provide the index?
[02:32] Alex: Good question. We host the embeddings inference - you post text and we return vectors. For storage Redwood customers typically integrate with their vector DB - we provide example pipelines for Pinecone, Milvus, Redis, or you can use an S3-backed ephemeral store for pilot. We don't force a managed vector DB.
[03:01] Samir: Ok, so for the pilot we'll probably use our existing Redis+vector plugin. Latency wise what should we expect for embedding generation?
[03:10] Priya: For short texts (like queries) it's usually sub-20ms p50 on our hosted models, p95 around 60-120ms depending on concurrency and batch size. For batches we can optimize throughput with our batch API which can push per-item cost down. The tradeoff is a bit higher tail latency.
[04:00] Mark: That p95 sounds optimistic, our traffic is spiky. How do you handle burst capacity?
[04:10] Alex: Hosted has autoscaling and we have burst capacity. For predictable heavy workloads customers often pick Dedicated, but Hosted can burst to handle short spikes. We also support routing by policy - you can route critical traffic to dedicated pools if you want lower tail latency.

[06:15] Priya: Demo time - I'm going to open the Console. (screen share) Here is the embeddings playground - you can paste sample text and see returned vectors. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"redwood inference API"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' Note: example keys shown are obfuscated.
[06:40] Janelle: Do you have a python SDK example for batch embeddings?
[06:45] Priya: Yes, we have a client with a batch_embed() helper and streaming options. We'll share the snippet after.

[09:00] Priya: Now the rerank flow - you pass the query and candidate documents (or candidate IDs and we fetch the text), plus optional metadata. The rerank endpoint returns a scored list with rationale. It's lower token cost because you're operating on top-k candidates instead of rerunning large generation.
[09:30] Mark: Can rerank use model-specific scoring? Like we want to weight recency and business score?
[09:36] Priya: You can pass metadata and a small prompt that includes business signals - the reranker can incorporate that. We also support custom scoring functions on the client side if you prefer deterministic weighting.

[12:00] Alex: Wanted to call out caching - we support prefix/K-V cache so repeated prefixes (like common query prefixes) can be served much faster. Note that sometimes our transcriptions say K-V case or K-V cache, we've had customers confuse that in notes :)
[12:14] Samir: Is that cache customer-configurable? Does it store embeddings or token-level outputs?
[12:20] Priya: It's on the model runtime side: KV cache holds transformer key/value states to speed up autoregressive generation. For embeddings/rerank the main cache is a prefix/candidate cache on the retrieval layer - you can configure TTLs and caching tiers. We'll share the docs.

[15:40] Mark: Security - we are SOC2 and ISO sensitive. Can you run in our VPC or on-prem?
[15:48] Alex: Yes, for regulated workloads we have Redwood Private - VPC deployments or an on-prem package. For Hosted we provide SOC2 reports, SSO/SAML, RBAC, customer-managed KMS integrations for key management on some plans. We'll push the security pack after.
[16:10] Janelle: What about data retention and audit logs?
[16:16] Priya: You can configure retention policies per-tenant and we expose audit logs in the Console and via APIs. We also support log forwarding to your SIEM.

[19:00] Samir: Any limits on token retention for embeddings? Like if we send customer PII, how do you handle it?
[19:07] Alex: We have options - by default hosted API may retain logs for debugging but we can opt out and disable retention for pilot, or use Private where data never leaves your VPC. We'll send the specific security docs for retention controls.

[22:00] Priya: Back to relevance - here's a quick example: query "waterproof hiking boots". First stage returns 200 candidates via vector similarity. We then call rerank with top 20 candidates plus product metadata and rerank model boosts products with recent sales and higher review scores. You can see how quality improves with rerank vs raw similarity.
[23:10] Mark: Can we quantify improvement? Do you have typical metrics?
[23:16] Priya: Sure, in our case studies we see relative NDCG improvements of 10-25% depending on dataset. For ecom with rich metadata you often get high gains because reranker can incorporate structured signals. We'll run a pilot benchmark on your sample queries to measure real numbers.

[26:30] Alex: On instrumentation - Console shows per-route latency, token counts, and cost breakdown by model. You can set SLO alerts and connect tracing hooks to your APM. This is helpful for spotting regressions when you change models or prompts.

[29:40] Janelle: About cost: if we do two-stage (embed + rerank) what's the typical cost profile?
[29:48] Priya: Embedding generation is per-text vector cost - cheap per query; rerank is a small generation-like call on top-k documents, so cost depends on tokens per candidate and k. For many customers rerank cost is cheaper than rescoring by full generation because it's targeted. We can show a cost calculator based on your qps and k.

[33:00] Samir: For the pilot we expect 50 qps average with spikes to 200 qps. Would hosted be fine?
[33:08] Alex: Hosted can handle that with autoscaling but tail latency during spikes may be higher. If you need strict p95 SLAs we'd recommend Dedicated. For pilot, Hosted is fine and faster to start.

[36:20] Mark: Integration complexity - how long does typical integration take?
[36:26] Priya: For a basic two-stage flow we see teams integrate and run initial benchmarks in 2-4 weeks. Full production + rollout with SLAs and A/B tests often takes 6-10 weeks depending on stakeholders.

[39:50] Priya: I'll demo a sample curl for rerank now. (screen) Example: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"query":"waterproof hiking boots","candidates":[{"id":"p1","text":"..."},...]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' The response includes score and explanation text.
[40:30] Janelle: Are there limits on payload size for candidate lists?
[40:36] Priya: We recommend top-k up to 100 but typical is 10-50. There are practical limits per request and the Console warns if payloads are large.

[43:00] Mark: Do you support A/B rollouts and automatic fallback if a model version regresses?
[43:06] Alex: Yes, Console supports canary/AB rollouts, and automatic fallback policies. If a new model causes a quality or latency regression the system can route back to the previous variant.

[46:20] Samir: Any gotchas with vector DB vendors? We use Redis vector today.
[46:26] Priya: Redis works well; just be mindful of consistency when you update embeddings and reindex. Our docs show an atomic reindex workflow. Also watch out for dimension mismatches and quantization differences if you use quantized vectors.

[49:50] Alex: Alright to wrap up - proposed pilot: 2-week benchmark using 1k queries + relevance labels, run on Hosted with a small concurrency profile, report NDCG and latency. If results look good, consider Dedicated for production.
[50:10] Mark: That works. We'll get the dataset to you.
[50:15] Janelle: Procurement timeline is around 6 weeks, so pilot sooner is better.

[51:00] Alex: Great - recap of next steps: I'll send pricing + security pack; Priya will share benchmark harness and samples; Samir to send dataset; Janelle to confirm stakeholders. We'll aim to kick off pilot the week of 2027-10-13.
[52:10] Mark: Thanks everyone.
[52:15] Samir: Thanks.
[52:20] Priya: Thanks all, we'll follow up via email with links and steps.
[52:25] Alex: Bye!

End of transcript.
